items.title: Robot swarms trained by trial and error in simulation keep working on real robots
items.summary: Reinforcement learning lets robots learn behaviors on their own, through trial and error, usually inside a computer simulation. Moving what they learn onto physical robots is another matter. Simulated and real robots never behave quite the same way, a mismatch known as the “reality gap,” and reinforcement learning has long been particularly sensitive to it. Researchers at IRIDIA, the artificial intelligence laboratory of the Université libre de Bruxelles (ULB), have shown how to get around it for robot swarms: swarms trained with their method in simulation keep performing reliably once they are moved onto real robots. Teaching a swarm of robots to search for survivors after an earthquake, or to explore a hostile site, entirely inside a computer before risking a real machine sounds like the sensible way to do it.
